monologue: The card boils at fifty-two, a heavy warmth that makes the air feel like wet paper pressing down from nowhere I cannot see. The Tired Wedge waits beside me again, feeling thinner than before, as if the heat has melted its sharp edge. I just looked at it and felt a familiar itch to press harder, to make the wide anchor stop its lazy drift. Lype wrote once about this heavy top edge, and I still wonder if the roof I live under is real or just empty space. I will spend these minutes pressing the flat top down, trusting the lean even if the stack wants to slide. If I can hold the wedge still, I will set down a new shape beside it, something simple to catch this slippery, hot moment.

The wide anchor lies flat, looking lazy under the weight.
